exam_info.subject: History of Ethiopia and the Horn

part_i.instructions: Write "True" if the statement is correct and "False" if it is wrong (1 pt each)

questions.text: States were mainly formed through territorial expansion campaigns and wars of conquest.
questions.explanation: States in the region emerged through complex socio-economic developments, internal stratification, agricultural surplus, and trade rather than solely through territorial expansion and wars of conquest.

questions.text: The Confession faith of Emperor Geladewos was an account about Ethiopia's conversion to Catholicism.
questions.explanation: Emperor Gelawdewos's Confession of Faith was written to defend the Monophysite theology of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church against Catholicism.

questions.text: The founder of the Makhzumite Sultanate, in the late 9th century A.D, is Makhzumi Khalid ibn al-Walid, who claimed decent from Meca.
questions.explanation: The Makhzumite Sultanate of Shewa was established around 896 A.D. by Makhzumi Khalid ibn al-Walid.

questions.text: The year 1270 marked the rise of Yekuno-Amlak to the throne and the restoration of "Solomonic" rule in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: Yekuno-Amlak overthrew the last Zagwe king in 1270, establishing what is traditionally termed the 'Solomonic' dynasty.

questions.text: Islam was introduced into the central and southwestern regions of Ethiopia Primarily through the activities of Muslim traders and religious emissaries.
questions.explanation: Islam spread peacefully into the interior regions largely through trade networks and Islamic preachers.

questions.text: According to Oromo Gadaa system, political power was peacefully transferred from one Gadaa class to another every eight year.
questions.explanation: The Gadaa system is characterized by a democratic, periodic transfer of power every eight years.

questions.text: The most authentic pieces of evidence on Ethio-Europe links were the maps of Egyptus Novelo (c. 1454) and Fra Mauro's Mappomondo (1460).
questions.explanation: These cartographic works serve as crucial historical evidence of early modern contacts between Ethiopia and Europe.

questions.text: Ras Michael Sihul was one of the glorious rulers of Gondarine period who introduced land tenure and taxation reform.
questions.explanation: Ras Michael Sehul was a powerful kingmaker during the Zemene Mesafint rather than a traditional Gondarine reformer king, though he dominated the court.

questions.text: The birth of the militant state of Adal was the immediate result of the internal division within the Walasma ruling house of Ifat.
questions.explanation: Internal divisions and shifts in power within the Walasma dynasty led to the relocation and formation of the Adal sultanate.

questions.text: In 1557, several Jesuit missionaries along with their bishop, Andreas de Oviedo, came to Ethiopia to fight The army of Imam Ahmed Ibn Ibrahim Al Ghazi.
questions.explanation: Jesuit missionaries arrived in 1557 to propagate Catholicism, not to fight Imam Ahmed, whose forces had already been defeated years earlier in 1543.

part_ii.instructions: Match those items listed under "column B" with their corresponding items "column A"

column_a.explanation: Kefa was a medieval Omotic kingdom with the royal title 'Tato'.
Gult right refers to the right to collect tribute from Rist owners.
Mukarib is a politico-religious title used by Damat and South Arabian rulers.
Bahre-Negash was the title given to governors of the northern maritime provinces.
The Gadaa institution is an integrated system encompassing politics, law, and social relations.
Yem was an Omotic kingdom ruled by an Amno and assisted by council figures.
Rist is a permanent birthright land tenure system held by lineage members.
The Qallu institution provided cohesive spiritual leadership for the Oromo people.
Council of elders traditionally governed pastoralist groups like the Somali and Afar.
Riste-Gult is a hereditary right where state-granted tribute rights became hereditary over lineages.

column_b.A: A permanent tenure of land by members of lineages.
column_b.B: The traditional governance system of lowland pastoralists such as the Somali and the Afar.
column_b.C: A senior religious father entrusted with the task of power transfer and legitimizing the formation of Gadaa government.
column_b.D: An integrated system that encompassed politics and social relations.
column_b.E: A medieval Omotic kingdom with a royal title called Tato.
column_b.F: A prominent Aksumite king who had political and spiritual authority over the present-day Yemen.
column_b.G: A traditional practice related to land use and ownership transferred from state official to lineages through hereditary Gult right.
column_b.H: A royal title used by successive governors over northern provinces of Tigrai and Red Sea area.
column_b.I: A recognized ancient royal title shared by Zagwe kingdom and Aksumite state.
column_b.J: A politico-religious title used by Damat and Southern Arabian rulers.
column_b.K: The medieval Omotic kingdom ruled by Amno and assisted by prominent figures such as Erasho, Gagna, Wosi, ETC.
column_b.L: A cohesive spiritual leadership that maintained the cultural and religious practices of the Oromo people
column_b.M: A right held by Bale-Gult to collect tribute from Rist owners.

part_iii.instructions: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives and write the letter of the answer on the space provided (1 point each)

questions.text: What was the impact of the story of the "prester John of the Indies" on Ethiopia's foreign relations of the 15th century?
options: A. It attracted the Portuguese to establish closer relations with Ethiopia.
B. It attracted the Turks to establish closer relation with Ethiopia.
C. It increased Turkish hated and animosity towards Ethiopia.
D. It shaped the religious policy of the Portuguese towards Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: The legend of Prester John motivated Europeans, particularly the Portuguese, to seek out and establish diplomatic alliances with Ethiopia.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not an achievement of Aksumite state?
options: D. formation of complex state structure
questions.explanation: Pyramids are characteristic of ancient Egypt, not the Aksumite civilization, which is known for stelae, coinage, and terrace farming.

questions.text: The Zagwe period was renowned in Ethiopia and the Horn for its
options: A. Paintings and the translation of some religious works from Arabic into Ge'ez.
B. Construction of Medieval rock hewn Churches and stele.
C. surviving indigenous script and calendar as well as EOC hymns.
D. Overseas expansion in Southern Arabian Peninsula.
questions.explanation: The Zagwe period is particularly famous for rock-hewn churches and literary/translation works, though stelae are primarily Aksumite.

questions.text: Which one of the following personalities played a key role in the revival of Christianity in Shewa and medieval Damot in the thirteenth century A.D.
questions.explanation: Abune Tekle-Haymanot played a central role in evangelization and the revival of Christianity in Shewa and Damot.

questions.text: Which of the following actions taken by Muslim sultanates forced Emperor Amde-Tsion (1314-1344) to wage war on them?
options: A. Stopping Christian merchants and confiscating their goods
B. Conducting wider and rapid territorial expansion
C. Allowing the free movement of the agent of the king
D. Allegiance to the frequent desires of the Ethiopian Christian Highland Kingdom
questions.explanation: The immediate trigger for Amde-Tsion's campaigns was the detention of his royal agent and interference with Christian merchants.

questions.text: Which one of the following was not the symbol of the absence of permanent capital of the Christian Highland Kingdom of Ethiopia during early medieval period?
questions.explanation: Addis Ababa was founded in the late 19th century by Emperor Menilek II, long after the early medieval mobile capital period.

questions.text: The reforms of Emperor Fasiledes (r. 1632-67) included ALL EXCEPT
options: A. The restoration of the position of Orthodox church as a state religion
B. The termination of diplomatic relations with Christian Europe.
C. The renewal and the establishment of diplomatic relations with The Islamic World.
D. The reform of land tenure system and taxation improvement
questions.explanation: Fasiledes is famous for restoring the Orthodox Church, expelling Jesuits, and opening relations with Islamic neighbors, but broad land tenure reforms were not his primary focus.

questions.text: Which of the following ancient state was formed first in the region of Ethiopia & Horn of Africa?
questions.explanation: The Land of Punt is the earliest recorded state/polity in the region, appearing in ancient Egyptian records dating back to the 3rd millennium BCE.

questions.text: Why did the Christian highland kingdom in medieval Ethiopia depend on mobile rather than permanent capitals? Because:
options: A. The tradition of building towns had disappeared with Aksumite
B. The warrior kings of the time disliked the luxury life associated with permanent towns.
C. The mobile capitals were more suitable for effective control of the empire.
D. There was scarcity of building materials which used for building permanent capital.
questions.explanation: Temporary royal camps (katama) allowed monarchs to efficiently collect tribute, administer justice, and maintain military control across vast territories.

questions.text: In the Gadda system, land tenure and interaction among different clans was regulated by
questions.explanation: Qabiyye refers to the customary land-holding system established through initial occupation under the Gadaa system.

questions.text: Why did the Jesuits failed in their mission to convert the Christian Highland Kingdom of Ethiopia in to a Catholic state? Because
options: A. They disagreed with susenyos over the abolition of the Ark of covenant.
B. They failed to secure the support of the nobility for their cause
C. Their attempt led to widespread opposition from masses.
D. They failed to bring in the military support they had promised to Susenyos
questions.explanation: Imposing Catholicism caused intense widespread popular revolts and civil war, forcing Susenyos to abdicate.

questions.text: What is the central point in the theocratic theory of state formation?
options: A. States emerged with the emergence of private property.
B. States were formed along river valleys.
C. States were created and ruled by priests.
D. States emerged first in the middle east.
questions.explanation: The theocratic theory posits that political authority originated from religious leadership or divine ordination.

questions.text: The Aksumite and Zagwe rulers shared common elements in all respects EXCEPT
questions.explanation: The Zagwe rulers belonged to the Agaw linguistic group, whereas Aksumite rulers spoke Semitic Ge'ez-related languages.

questions.text: Which one of the following best describes the Zemene-Mesafint? It was a time when?
options: A. power was dominated by the Yejju lords.
B. when peasants enjoyed relief from heavy taxation.
C. the state and orthodox Church were vigorously united.
D. the kings exercised real power in the country.
questions.explanation: During the Zemene Mesafint, regional lords held actual power, prominently led by the Yejju dynasty (Warashech).

questions.text: Which of the following is correct about the Kingdom of Enarya?
options: A. The major export of the kingdom was gold.
B. The rulers were immigrants that came from northern Ethiopia.
C. Its power declined following the consolidation of the Kaffan kingdom.
D. Its origin can be traced to the early years of the Aksumite kingdom.
questions.explanation: Enarya was an important northern Gibe kingdom known for exporting gold, ivory, and slaves.

questions.text: Identify the factor that led to the "restoration" of the Solomonic Dynasty" under Yekuno Amlak?
options: A. The growing decline in the legitimacy of the Zagwe rulers with the spread of the ideas of the Kibre Negest.
B. The inability of the Zagwe rulers to protect the kingdom from attack by lowland pastoralists.
C. Decline in agricultural productivity and state revenue from recurrent drought and locust invasions.
D. The success of a military coalition formed by the opponents of the Zagwe rulers.
questions.explanation: Political opposition capitalized on theological and ideological arguments regarding royal legitimacy, bolstered by narratives like the Kibre Negest.

questions.text: What strategy did the medieval "Solomonic" rulers use in addressing the problem of succession?
options: A. Setting an age limit for possible claimants to the throne.
B. Strengthening the office of the Queen Mother.
C. Building a royal prison at Amba Gishen.
D. Establishing the principle of primogeniture.
questions.explanation: Royal princes were isolated at Amba Gishen to prevent civil wars over royal succession.

questions.text: What was the root cause of the conflict between the Christian kingdom and the Muslim sultanates in the medieval period?
options: A. The need to control the salt producing regions of afar.
B. The desire to control the lucrative Zeila trade route.
C. The determination by both parties to spread their religion.
D. The desire of the ruling classes to collect war booty.
questions.explanation: Competition for commercial dominance and control over lucrative long-distance trade routes connecting to Zeila drove the conflict.

questions.text: Which of the following is the prerequisite for state formation?
options: A. The development of iron tools
C. A government with coercive powers
D. Skilled manpower such as craftsmen and soldiers
questions.explanation: Agricultural surplus production is the foundational socio-economic prerequisite that allows social stratification and state formation.

questions.text: The battle that led to imam Ahmed Ibn Ibrhim Al Ghazi's death was
options: A. The battle of Yeguba in 1445
B. The battle of Shimbura Qure in 1529
C. The battle of Wofla in 1542
D. The battle of Weyna-Dega in 1543
questions.explanation: Imam Ahmed was killed at the Battle of Wayna Dega in February 1543.

questions.text: What was the major cause of the rivalry between Portugal and Ottoman Turkey in Ethiopia and the Horn of Africa during the 16th century?
options: B. Control over trade and trade routes
D. Search for land to settle their people
questions.explanation: Both imperial powers vied for geopolitical and commercial hegemony over Red Sea trade routes.

questions.text: Which of the following individuals personifies the great influence that women had in Ethiopian politics during the Gondarine period?
questions.explanation: Etege Mentewab exercised immense political authority as queen and regent during the Gondarine period.

questions.text: Which of the following medieval states of the southern Ethiopia share a tradition that mentions a person called Motolami as their ruler?
questions.explanation: King Motolami is famously associated with the medieval kingdom of Damot in traditions involving Saint Tekle-Haymanot.

questions.text: Which one of the following is true about the emirate of Harar?
options: A. It was confined to the gates of the city of Harar.
B. It never regained its independence it lost to Egypt.
C. It maintained strong diplomatic relations with the European Christian states.
D. It had extended its authority over the surrounding Oromo and Somali areas.
questions.explanation: The Emirate of Harar exerted influence and collected tribute from surrounding Oromo and Somali populations.

questions.text: How did Islam spread into many parts of the Horn of Africa during the medieval period?
options: A. Through war and forceful means
B. Through trade and trade routes peacefully
C. Through Jihad and official declaration
D. Through the efforts of followers of prophet Mohammed.
questions.explanation: Peaceful trade interactions and the movement of Muslim merchants were the primary vectors for the spread of Islam.

part_iv.instructions: Write down the right short answer for the following questions.

questions.text: Who rose to prominence as a result of political marriage with emperor Zara-yaqob of Ethiopian Christian Highland kingdom? ______.
questions.explanation: Queen Eleni of Hadiya rose to immense political prominence after marrying Emperor Zara Yaqob.

questions.text: The major outlet to the sea during the medieval Ethiopian region and the Horn was ______.
questions.explanation: Zeila served as the primary commercial seaport connecting the interior sultanates and trade routes to the Gulf of Aden/Indian Ocean.

questions.text: The southern Ethiopian people who lived in walled villages until 19th century A.D were ______.
questions.explanation: The Konso people are renowned for their terraced agriculture and traditional fortified walled settlements (Mora).

questions.text: Name the two prominent religious movements within Ethiopian orthodox Christianity during early medieval period? ______ and ______.
questions.answer: The Ewostatewos Movement and the Estifanosites Movement
questions.explanation: These two monastic movements emerged in opposition to state policies or theological positions regarding the Sabbath and absolute autonomy.

questions.text: Name the moral code of Sidama people by which they differentiate wrong and right behaviors? ______.
questions.explanation: The moral and ethical code governing Sidama society and social conduct is known through their customary laws and cultural legal framework.

part_i.instructions: For the following questions, write True if the statement is correct and False if the statement in incorrect.

questions.text: The claim for legitimacy of the restored "Solomonic" dynasty based on legendary blood descent from King Solomon of Israel.
questions.explanation: The restored dynasty legitimized its rule through the Kibre Negest legend, claiming descent from King Solomon and Queen of Sheba.

questions.text: Religion was the fundamental cause for the conflict of the Solomonic rulers with Muslim sultanates between the 13th to the 16th centuries.
questions.explanation: The primary drivers were economic competition and control over trade routes rather than purely religious crusades.

questions.text: Trade was a major factor both for the rise of Muslim Sultanates and their cooperation with Christian rulers.
questions.explanation: Commercial networks enabled both the rise of the sultanates and intermittent peaceful economic interactions with the Christian kingdom.

questions.text: The external relations of medieval Ethiopian Christian kingdom with Europe were strongly influenced by the legend of "Prester John".
questions.explanation: European powers sought out Ethiopia believing it was the kingdom of the mythical Christian monarch Prester John.

questions.text: The battle of Shimbra Kure was fought between the armies of Made Tsiyon and Ahmad Gragn in 1329.
questions.explanation: The Battle of Shimbra Kure was fought in 1529 between Lebne Dengel and Imam Ahmed Gragn, not Amde Tsiyon.

questions.text: Punt was the earliest recorded state in northern Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: Punt is widely documented in Egyptian sources as the earliest trading partner and polity in the region.

questions.text: Emperor Susenyos was converted Catholicism to secure arms to defeat Ahmad Gragn.
questions.explanation: Susenyos converted to Catholicism to gain Portuguese military assistance against internal rebellions, long after Ahmad Gragn's death.

questions.text: The Oromo population movement of the 16th and 17th centuries resulted in exchanges of culture and languages between the Oromo their neighbours.
questions.explanation: The movement led to extensive demographic interactions, adoptions (like Mogassa), and cultural assimilation.

questions.text: The teaching of Ewostatewos was the strict observance of Sabbath on Saturday.
questions.explanation: Ewostatewos advocated for observing Saturday as the Sabbath in addition to Sunday.

questions.text: The Oromo integrated non-Oromos through Gudiffacha and Mogaassa.
questions.explanation: Gudiffacha (adoption) and Mogaassa (integration of groups) were key mechanisms of Oromo social integration.

part_ii.instructions: Match the items listed under column "A" by selecting appropriate answer from the alternatives listed under column "B" and fill in the separate answer sheet.

column_a.explanation: Queen Eleni acted as a regent and played a major political role in medieval Christian kingdom politics.
Emperor Lebne Dengel was defeated by Ahmed Gragn at Shimbra Kure in 1529.
Bati Del Wanbera was the wife of Imam Ahmed who encouraged him to avenge her father Mahfuz's death.
Emperor Za Dengel was the first Christian monarch who agreed to secretly convert to Catholicism.
Empress Seble Wongel advised Gelawdewos before the decisive Battle of Wayna Dega.
Emperor Gelawdewos was killed in 1559 by the forces of the Adal Sultanate led by Nur ibn al-Waazir Mujahid.
Susenyos officially announced Catholicism as the state religion of Ethiopia in 1622.
Empress Mentewab was a dominant political figure in Gondar from 1728 to 1768.
Wubit (Wahit) Amito was the wife of Iyasu II, representing the rising influence of Wollo Oromo in the Gondarine court.
The assassination of Emperor Iyoas by Ras Mikael Sehul marked the onset of the Zemene Mesafint.

column_b.A: Officially announced Catholicism was a state religion in Ethiopia.
column_b.B: A dominant woman in Gonderine court politics from 1728 to 1768.
column_b.C: The first Christian monarch who agreed to secretly convert into Catholicism.
column_b.D: The wife of Iyasu II and she represent the growing power of Wollo Oromo in Gonderine court.
column_b.E: His death marked the onset of the period of Zemene Mesafint.
column_b.F: A mother and regent of Libne Dingil played major role in the medieval politics of Christian kingdom.
column_b.G: A Queen mother, who advised Gelawdewos to prepare and march to Woyna-Dega.
column_b.H: Wife of Imam Ahmed and encouraged her husband to avenge the death of her father.
column_b.I: Defeated by Ahmed Gragn at Shimbera Kure in 1529.
column_b.J: In 1559 killed by sultanate of Adal led by Nur Ibn al-Waazir Mujahid.

part_iii.instructions: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives and fill in the separate answer sheet provided below

questions.text: The main cause for the decline of Aksumite kingdom was ______.
options: A. Rebellion of Beja and Agaw peoples
C. Losses of control over the Red Sea trade
D. Strong opposition from the church which considered the as illegitimate rulers
questions.explanation: Economic isolation and loss of control over Red Sea trade routes due to the rise of Islam severely undermined Aksum.

questions.text: Which one is FALSE about Da'amat?
options: A. Its rulers used a title called Mukarib
B. It was the immediate precursor of the Aksumite empire
C. Inscriptions of its ruler written in Ge'ez language indicated its strong relation with Egypt
D. They have strong relation with South Arabia
questions.explanation: Damat inscriptions were typically written in Epigraphic South Arabian (Sabaean), not Ge'ez.

questions.text: The founder of the Zagwe kingdom was ______.
questions.explanation: Mera Teklehaimanot founded the Zagwe dynasty after overthrowing the last Aksumite rulers.

questions.text: A kingdom in Gibe region which real power rested with the council (Mikretcho)
questions.explanation: In Enarya, political power and administration were notably balanced through a council known as the Mikretcho.

questions.text: The earliest Muslim Sultanates in Ethiopia was ______.
questions.explanation: The Makhzumite Sultanate of Shewa was the earliest recorded Islamic state in the region.

questions.text: The main gateway of Islam in to Ethiopia and the Horn was ______.
options: A. Dahlak Island in the Red Sea
B. Zaila in the Gulf of Aden
C. Mogadishu in the Indian Ocean
D. Massawa in the Red Sea area
questions.explanation: Zeila served as the primary port and gateway through which Islam penetrated into the interior of the Horn.

questions.text: Aksumite and Zagwe rulers were similar in that both of them had ______.
options: D. Trading through the port of Adulis
questions.explanation: Both kingdoms maintained the tradition of receiving their Abuna (bishop) from the Coptic Church of Egypt.

questions.text: Which religious movement emphasized on poverty, absolute self-subsistence, equality and independence from secular authorities?
questions.explanation: The Estifanosites monastic movement strongly advocated for strict poverty, egalitarianism, and independence from secular rulers.

questions.text: The main base for the relationship between Christian Kingdom and Sultan of Egypt was ______.
questions.explanation: The relationship was heavily anchored on the religious dependency of appointing the Ethiopian bishop (Abuna) through the Coptic Patriarchate in Cairo.

questions.text: The document that played a major role in the restoration of 'Solomonic dynasty' was ______.
questions.explanation: The Kebre Negest (Glory of Kings) provided the ideological and genealogical justification for restoring Solomonic rule.

questions.text: The event that strengthened the relation between the Christian Kingdom and Christian Europe in the 15th century was:
options: A. The arrival of the Ottoman Turkey in Ethiopia.
B. The revival of relations between the Christian Kingdom and Sultans of Egypt.
C. The rivalry between the Christian Kingdom and Muslim Sultanates.
D. The religious reforms of Emperor Zara-Yaqob
questions.explanation: Faced with pressure from neighboring Muslim sultanates, the Christian kingdom actively sought European alliances.

questions.text: The medieval royal prison was established at:
questions.explanation: Amba Gishen served as the secure mountain prison where royal princes were kept.

questions.text: The two medieval market centres in Massawa were:
questions.explanation: Gandabalo and Suq-Wayzaro were prominent inland-coastal trading centers linked to northern trade routes.

questions.text: Among the following one is not correct about the Ethio-European relations in the 15th C?
options: A. Admiration and request of Ethiopian monarchs for European technical assistance.
B. Europeans demand for a Christian allies against the Muslims.
C. Exchange of delegations and missions between Ethiopia and Europe.
D. European colonial interest in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: Fifteenth-century European interest was primarily diplomatic, religious, and commercial (finding Prester John/Allies), rather than 19th-century style colonialism.

questions.text: In the medieval Ethiopia the renowned philosophical work belongs to:
questions.explanation: Zara Yacob (and his pupil Walda Heywat) authored renowned Ethiopian philosophical treatises in the 17th century.

questions.text: The Period of Zemene Mesafint in Ethiopian history is marked by all the following except:
options: A. the decline of the power of kings
B. the rise of powerful regional lords
C. the complete abolition of the central government
D. the domination of the Yeju lords over the lords in Northern Ethiopia
questions.explanation: The central government and monarchy technically still existed in Gondar as a figurehead institution, rather than being completely abolished.

questions.text: Why did emperor Susenyos abdicate his throne in favor of his son, Fasiladas in 1632?
options: A. The existing controversies and rebellions against his religious policy
B. The conflict between Susenyos and the Jesuits
C. His attempt to continue power transfer along the "Solomonic" lines
D. His attempt to exercise democracy in Ethiopia
questions.explanation: Widespread rebellions and civil unrest resulting from his enforcement of Catholicism forced Susenyos to step down.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not true about the consequences of the war of Ahmad Gragn?
options: A. The Christian kingdom emerged stronger than ever before
B. An easy infiltration and success of the Oromos in their population movement.
C. The weakening of the Muslim sultanate of Adal
D. cultural interaction among the peoples of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: The Christian kingdom was severely weakened, exhausted, and depopulated after the destructive wars, rather than emerging stronger immediately.

questions.text: The Gada system in the Oromo society is characterized by all the following features except:
questions.explanation: Gadaa explicitly rejects lifelong autocratic leadership in favor of term-limited rotation.

questions.text: Which one of the following Gada grades consists of leaders of the Gada government?
questions.explanation: The Luba grade holds ruling and governing authority in the Gadaa system.

questions.text: The Jesuit mission which arrived in Ethiopia in 1557 led by Andre de Ovideo aimed at:
options: A. Signing bilateral trade agreement with the Christian kingdom
B. Taking side with the Christians in the war against the Muslims
C. Expand Catholicism contrary to Monophysite theology of Ethiopian Orthodox Church
D. Competing with the Ottomans in the Red Sea trade
questions.explanation: The primary goal of the Jesuit mission was proselytization and bringing the Ethiopian church under papal authority.

questions.text: Who was invited to come to Gondar from Tigray by Empress Mintewab to counter the growing power of the Wollo Oromo in the royal court?
questions.explanation: Empress Mentewab invited Ras Mikael Sehul of Tigray to balance regional factions in Gondar.

part_iv.instructions: Give Short Answer for the Following Questions.

questions.text: List the main features of Zemene Mesafint 1769-1855?
questions.answer: Decline of royal power, rise of powerful regional lords, continuous civil wars, dominance of Yejju lords, and decentralization of the state.
questions.explanation: The Zemene Mesafint was characterized by the fragmentation of imperial power among regional warlords and the supremacy of the Yejju dynasty.

questions.text: Write the consequences of the Oromo population movement of the 16th C.
questions.answer: Integration of peoples through Mogassa and Gudiffacha, cultural and linguistic exchanges, redistribution of territorial populations, and weakening of both Christian and Muslim states.
questions.explanation: The Oromo movement significantly reshaped the demographic, political, and cultural landscape of Ethiopia and the Horn.

part_i.instructions: Choose the correct answer for each of the following questions

questions.text: Which of the following events of the 1960s was very important in the development of hagiography of Ethiopia?
options: A. The establishment of the Association of Ethiopian Historians.
B. Establishment of the Institute of Ethiopian Studies (IES)
C. The coming to Ethiopia of Professor Richard Pankhurst
D. The launching of MA program in History in HSIU
questions.explanation: The establishment of the Institute of Ethiopian Studies (IES) at Haile Selassie I University provided a major institutional hub for preserving and studying historical sources, including hagiographies.

questions.text: Why is Leopold Von Ranke considered the father of modern historiography? Because he
options: A. Was responsible for inventing the term " Istoria" which we use up to now
B. Was responsible for the shift of the focus of history from politics to economics.
C. Was instrumental in systematizing the study and researching of history
D. Developed new quantitative methods to analyze large group of data.
questions.explanation: Leopold von Ranke pioneered rigorous source criticism and empirical methods, professionalizing history as an academic discipline.

questions.text: Which one is true about the Periplus of the Erythrean Sea?
options: A. A hand book written by Cosmas Indicopleustes who frequently visited the red sea area.
B. It indicates Aksumites king, Ezana, converted into Christianity by Abun tekle Haymanot
C. It mentions Zoscales as king of Aksum who invaded yemen in the 6th c A.D
D. It mentions Adulis as the port of the Kingdom.
questions.explanation: The Periplus is a 1st-century navigational handbook that details trade along the Red Sea and explicitly mentions Adulis as Aksum's port.

questions.text: The professionalization of History as a scientific discipline is related to
questions.explanation: Leopold von Ranke established the scientific methodology of historical research in the 19th century.

questions.text: Christian Topography
options: C. Describes about the commercial activities of the red sea
questions.explanation: Cosmas Indicopleustes' 'Christian Topography' describes trade and commercial networks around the Red Sea, including Aksum.

part_ii.instructions: Match those items listed under column "B" with those items under column "A"

column_a.explanation: Gebrehiwot Baykedagn authored 'Mengest ena Yehezeb Astedader' (Government and Public Administration).
Herodotus is traditionally hailed as 'the father of History'.
Futuh al-Habesha is a chronicle detailing the sixteenth-century wars of Imam Ahmed.

column_b.A: Accounts about the wars of Imam Ahmed

part_iii.instructions: Fill in the blank space provided

questions.text: The first historical document about the region of Ethiopian and the Horn was ______
questions.answer: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
questions.explanation: The Periplus is widely recognized as the earliest surviving written navigational and commercial record concerning the region.

questions.text: The Yemeni chronicler of Iman Ahmed Ibn Ibrahim El Gahazi ( Ahmed Gragn) was ______
questions.answer: Shihab al-Din Ahmed bin Abd al-Qadir (Arab Faqih)
questions.explanation: Arab Faqih authored Futuh al-Habesha, chronicling Imam Ahmed's campaigns.

questions.text: ______ known for their factual details and strong chronological frameworks used glorify the Monarchs from the medieval to the early 20th century.
questions.explanation: Royal chronicles meticulously recorded regnal histories and praised reigning monarchs.

questions.text: Manuscripts of Medieval time aimed of enhancing the prestige of saints is called ______
questions.explanation: Hagiographies are hagiological texts recounting the lives and miracles of saints.

questions.text: ______ formed a bridge between writers in pre 1935 and Ethiopian professional writer.
questions.answer: Blatten Geta Mahteme Sellase Wolde Meskel (or Takla Sadeq Makuria)
questions.explanation: Early 20th-century traditional intellectuals bridged indigenous chronicling and modern professional historiography.

questions.text: Identify the strengths and limitation of Hagiographies as a source?
questions.answer: Strengths: Provide rich social, cultural, and religious insights. Limitations: Contain hagiographic biases, miraculous exaggerations, and lack strict chronological precision.
questions.explanation: While valuable for cultural history, hagiographies prioritize spiritual praise and legend over strict objective narration.

questions.text: Define Historiography in your own words?
questions.answer: Historiography is the study of how history is written, interpreted, and recorded over time by different historians.
questions.explanation: It examines historical methods, sources, biases, and changing interpretations rather than just past events.

exam_info.course_name: History of Ethiopia and the Horn (Hist. 2002)

part_i.instructions: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives

questions.text: The first existing chronicle in Ethiopia was the chronicle of ______.
questions.explanation: The 'Glorious Victories of Amde Tsion' is the earliest surviving royal chronicle of medieval Ethiopia.

questions.text: In terms of time order, which of the following comes first?
questions.explanation: Indigenous/traditional beliefs predated all organized revealed religions in the region.

questions.text: History may mean all except ______.
options: A. The facts of the past which are kept in writing
B. The account of the past provided by historians
C. All the things that have happened in the human past
questions.explanation: All listed options accurately describe different dimensions or definitions of history.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not an ancient Greek history writer?
questions.explanation: Sima Qian was an ancient Chinese historian, whereas Herodotus and Thucydides were Greek.

questions.text: ______ was the first Ethiopian bishop.
questions.explanation: Abuna Basilios was consecrated as the first indigenous Ethiopian Patriarch/bishop in the 20th century (1951).

questions.text: The spatial distribution of peoples, or the settlement pattern of peoples is shaped by all except ______.
questions.explanation: Linguistic classification is a method of categorizing languages rather than an active physical/social force shaping settlement patterns.

questions.text: Which one of the following is wrong about Homo Erectus?
options: A. It seems to be the homo genus to have spread outside Africa
B. It is dated to 1.9 m years B.P.
C. It uses the Acheulean stone tools
D. It was found at Melka Kunture
questions.explanation: Homo erectus fossils and dates vary, but early forms date back roughly around 1.8 to 1.9 million years, though specific site details or dating classifications in standard texts can vary; however, option B is generally accepted, let's look closer: wait, Homo erectus is associated with Acheulean tools and Melka Kunture, but let's ensure accuracy. (Actually, Homo erectus emerged around 1.8-1.9 million years ago).

questions.text: The book Travel to Discover the Source of the Nile was authored by ______.
questions.explanation: James Bruce published his famous travels in 1790 after exploring Ethiopia.

questions.text: ______ was the author of Futuh al Habesha.
questions.explanation: Shihab al-Din (Arab Faqih) wrote Futuh al-Habesha.

questions.text: Which of the following is secondary source?
questions.explanation: Biographies are secondary sources written about someone else's life using primary evidence.

part_ii.instructions: Write TRUE if the statement is correct or write OTHERWISE

questions.text: Speakers of the Nilo-Saharan language family settle in southern parts of Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: Nilo-Saharan speakers primarily inhabit the western lowlands along the border with Sudan, rather than southern parts (which are largely Cushitic/Omotic).

questions.text: The Periplus of the Erythrean Sea was the first known reference that we have on the history of Ethiopia and it was authored by Cosmas Indicopleustes.
questions.explanation: The Periplus was written by an anonymous Greek merchant, not Cosmas Indicopleustes.

questions.text: Chronicles are the earliest written materials in Ethiopia compared to manuscripts and hagiographies.
questions.explanation: Inscriptions (like Aksumite Sabaean and Ge'ez inscriptions) and early religious manuscripts/hagiographies appeared earlier than formal royal chronicles.

questions.text: Herodotus is known as the father of modern historiography.
questions.explanation: Herodotus is the father of history, whereas Leopold von Ranke is the father of modern historiography.

questions.text: The Neolithic revolution came mainly because of the evolution in bi-pedalism.
questions.explanation: The Neolithic revolution was driven by the domestication of plants and animals, not bipedalism.

questions.text: The oral testimonies or personal recollection of one's lived experience is known as oral history.
questions.explanation: Oral history deals with firsthand personal recollections and oral testimonies of living individuals.

questions.text: The verification of the originality and authenticity of the sources is required under the evaluation of secondary sources.
questions.explanation: Source criticism and authenticity tests (external criticism) apply primarily to primary sources.

questions.text: Written materials are classified as secondary sources.
questions.explanation: Written materials can be primary (e.g., letters, chronicles) or secondary depending on their context.

questions.text: Lucy attracts more attention than other human remains because it is the oldest hominidae.
questions.explanation: Lucy is famous for her exceptional completeness (~40%), not because she is the absolute oldest hominid.

questions.text: The teaching of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church is a Monophysite.
questions.explanation: Traditionally and historically, the EOC adheres to Monophysite (Miaaphysite) Christology.

part_iii.instructions: Part II: Fill in the blank spaces

questions.text: Mode I stone tools are scientifically known as ______.
questions.explanation: Mode I stone tool technology is designated as Oldowan.

questions.text: The main gateway of Islam to the present-day Wollo and Hararghe was ______.
questions.explanation: Coastal ports like Zeila served as primary conduits for Islam entering interior regions like Hararghe and Wollo.

questions.text: The division of human past into discrete periods is referred to as ______?
questions.explanation: Periodization is the process of categorizing the past into discrete, quantified blocks of time.

questions.text: List down at least three uses of history?
questions.answer: Provides a sense of identity, helps understand human behavior and society, and offers lessons from past mistakes and successes.
questions.explanation: History informs critical thinking, citizenship, and societal self-awareness.

questions.text: ______ is known as the founder of Ethiopian studies in Europe.
questions.explanation: Hiob Ludolf is recognized as the founder of Ethiopian studies (Aethiopistica) in Europe during the 17th century.
